title: Increase Permissible Interstate Speed Limit
lastAction: Ref to the Com on Transportation, if favorable, State and Local Government, if favorable, Judiciary 1, if favorable, Rules, Calendar, and Operations of the House
aiSummary: This bill increases the maximum allowable speed limit on North Carolina interstate highways and controlled-access highways from 70 miles per hour to 75 miles per hour. It also updates related traffic enforcement penalties and license suspension thresholds to align with the new higher speed limit.
aiProArguments: Supporters argue that increasing interstate speed limits reflects modern driving conditions and vehicle safety capabilities, potentially reducing congestion by allowing traffic to flow more freely. They contend that many drivers already travel at these speeds, so the change brings regulations in line with actual driving behavior and may improve traffic efficiency on major highways.
aiConArguments: Opponents argue that higher speed limits increase accident risk and severity, particularly in poor weather conditions or heavy traffic. They express concern about public safety and note that higher speeds reduce reaction time and increase fuel consumption, and that the change primarily benefits those who can afford newer, safer vehicles while putting all road users at greater risk.
